tasks.desc: Ideation and approach selection: use one-dimensional cut-path DP instead of the 2D exact-count DP.
Implement the one-dimensional O(n^2) cut-path DP with prefix sums and the p>0 internal-cut penalty, returning dp[n] + k*totalCost.
Verify correctness on the two examples, n=1, one-subarray, all-singletons, and small random brute-force partitions.
Finalize the solution in the provided starter code with Python integer arithmetic and O(n^2) runtime.

proposals: Try the one-dimensional cut-path DP first: compute prefix sums, run an O(n^2) minimum over previous cuts using the suffix-cost edge weight, add the global k*totalCost constant, and verify on the examples and edge cases n=1, all one piece, and all singletons.

If an O(n) or O(n log n) method is desired, accelerate the one-dimensional DP with a monotone convex hull or Li Chao tree, treating each previous cut as a line in prefixNum[r] and querying in increasing prefixNum order.

Implement the supplied two-dimensional DP over the exact number of subarrays with a monotone convex hull as an independent fallback, keeping only previous and current rows and taking the minimum final value over all possible subarray counts.

Try a divide-and-conquer DP optimization for the two-dimensional DP based on the Monge property of the transition, if convex-hull implementation proves fragile, while carefully restricting previous-cut ranges to valid nonempty partitions.
Use a small brute-force enumerator over all partitions or a naive O(n^3) DP on tiny random inputs to cross-check any of the optimized formulations before finalizing.
prev: Implement the one-dimensional O(n^2) cut-path DP: build prefix sums prefNum and prefCost, set dp[0]=0, for each r=1..n compute dp[r] = min over p<r of dp[p] + prefNum[r]*(prefCost[r]-prefCost[p]) + (k*(prefCost[n]-prefCost[p]) if p>0 else 0), then return dp[n] + k*prefCost[n]; run the two provided examples and edge cases n=1, one subarray, and all singletons.
